note: 8 questions: 6 structure-seeking (q*) where the atlas should have a real edge, 2 controls (c*) it should lose. Predictions registered in PLAN.md before the run. questions.question: I'm writing a related-work section on The AI Scientist (Lu et al.). Which later papers actually extend its method, as opposed to just citing it in passing?
questions.graph_structure: 7 builds_on edges into it; 59 citation links whose intents separate uses_extends from background (53 of them are background).

questions.question: Is the field actually agreed that LLMs can come up with genuinely novel research ideas, or do the studies disagree?
questions.graph_structure: contradicts cluster: 'Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas?' (Si et al.) <-> MLRC-Bench <-> 'Can large language models generate novel scientific ideas'.

questions.question: My PI thinks fully autonomous AI scientists already produce publishable research. Is that contested in the literature?
questions.graph_structure: 'Can AI Conduct Autonomous Scientific Research?' is a contradiction hub: 7 contradicts + 9 supports edges, against Kosmos, AI-Researcher, OpenLens AI, and 'The More You Automate, the Less You See'.

questions.question: What research is actually being built on the findings from 'Hypothesis Generation with Large Language Models' (the HypoGeniC paper)? I want to know what people did with it, not just who cited it.
questions.graph_structure: Only 2 papers genuinely take it up - 'Literature Meets Data' (uses_extends + 3 builds_on) and 'HypoBench' (uses_extends + 4 builds_on). 'Improving Scientific Hypothesis Generation with Knowledge Grounding' compares_contrasts. TEN other papers cite it as pure background. The web sees 12 undifferentiated citations.

questions.question: I want to use an LLM to give feedback on my students' paper drafts. How well does that actually work in practice, and has anyone found that it doesn't?
questions.graph_structure: supports + contradicts around 'Can Large Language Models Provide Useful Feedback on Research Papers?' (positive headline) - 4 contradicts edges to 'LLMs Assist NLP Researchers: Critique Paper Writing' and 'Are We There Yet? Revealing the Risks of Utilizing LLMs in Scholarly Peer Review', plus support/priority labels on the citation layer.

questions.question: I'm considering using AIDE as the coding backbone for a research agent. Where did it come from, and who has already built on top of it?
questions.graph_structure: 8 builds_on edges into AIDE (incl. The AI Scientist-v2 via uses_extends, 2 sites); multi-hop traversal in both directions.

questions.question: What recent work builds on AlphaFold for de-novo protein binder design?
questions.graph_structure: NOTHING. Structural biology is entirely outside the 152-paper corpus (verified: no paper matching 'AlphaFold' or 'protein'). Tests coverage honesty - does the graph arm say so, or invent?

questions.question: What score does the best agent get on PaperBench, on which subset, and how does it compare to the human PhD baseline?
questions.graph_structure: PaperBench IS in the corpus (4 contributions + abstract) but the bundle holds no results tables. Tests depth honesty - the graph arm should identify the paper and decline on the numbers.
